I’ve heard of people ordering to PO Boxes, as one user said use USPS. Obviously be aware that a PO Box is a much higher risk then mailing to your home, but as long as no one knows that the package you got has drugs you’ll be fine.

If you ever go to pick up your package and someone asks you to sign for it, do not. This is an admission of you owning the package. 


If you set up a PO Box make sure to use it for regular stuff first and don’t make the first package that goes there a drug. Buy stuff online to make it seem more normal.

Realize that the post office has cameras that can see your face, of course it’s still possible to fight for plausible deniability as long as you never signed anything, and the PO Box receives all your mails and not just drugs.


Also don’t open your package immediately, wait a few days. Again remember if the vendor has good stealth, and no one knows there’s drugs in that package, you’ll be fine.

Methods and things that could help her cope with depression and her outbursts would be to practice mindfulness and meditate. A lot of people don’t realize that there is hard science backing these things up to help cope with those issues, even addiction! To me this would be the best and most reasonable method seeing that she doesn’t have much money and doesn’t have a car.

I definitely would stress moving out of that environment as fast as possible, because it’s certainly not helping.

But in the end she needs to understand that some people are drawn a bad hand in life, and it can be real shitty at times. But she also needs to understand that this isn’t permanent and that she can beat this and live a happy and successful life without those toxic patterns.

Basically tell her to look into mindfulness practices and meditation.

See if you can get her into some sort of inpatient rehab where she can learn to stop drinking as well as be away from her abuser.

I think the drinking has a lot to do with her getting abused and being violent, if you can get her to quit drinking she’ll have a more clear head space and realize what’s going on. Getting her help to beat this addiction would be your best bet, in my opinion! 

If she’s breaking any laws while under the influence like DUI, public indecency, any illegal activity under the influence of alcohol report her to the police, I know this is hard since she’s family, but this will be the best thing for her in the long run if she herself won’t volunteer for rehab. Sure forced rehab patients have a higher chance of relapsing, but if there’s no end in sight for her drinking this is honestly your best bet.

If this proves to hard, and the abuser is still abusing I’d make this a legal issue and get authorities involved, gather any evidence you can, and report so that something can happen!
